reasoning: Working through the causal chain: 1) TARGET ENGAGEMENT: There is evidence of target engagement - NIS expression increased from 21% to 25% (median) and NIS mRNA expression increased, indicating the drug reached and modulated its intended target (histone deacetylase leading to NIS re-expression). 2) PATHWAY MODULATION: The downstream biology partially moved as predicted - NIS expression was restored, which was the intended biological effect of HDAC inhibition. 3) CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite biological activity, the clinical endpoint failed - 10/13 patients showed no radioactive iodine uptake post-treatment, and 6/8 patients in Phase 2 had progressive disease with only 1/8 achieving stable disease. 4) POPULATION EFFECTS: No clear subgroup responders identified. 5) CONFOUNDERS: The trial appears adequately designed with appropriate duration (16 weeks) and dosing. This represents a classic 'biology moved but endpoint flat' pattern where target engagement and some downstream biology occurred but didn't translate to the intended clinical benefit.
